origins.section: The Interface's Parameter Types Choose the Overload; the Value at Run Time Doesn't
An Exact Reference Lets javac Pick `submit(Callable)`; Overloading the Method Makes the Call Ambiguous
An Exact Reference Lets javac Pick `submit(Callable)`; Overloading the Method Makes the Call Ambiguous
An Inexact Method Reference Leaves Inference Without the Types It Needs
A Varargs Method Packs the Interface's Arguments, So an Array Becomes One Element

recorded.pass:q-formatter-map: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-formatter-map: The first code block declares `Function<Object, String> fromObject = String::valueOf;` and its output line `A-7 | [C@7f31245a` shows it prints `[C@` and a hash for a char[]; the prose says it was resolved at compile time and `fromObject calls valueOf(Object) whatever it is given`.

recorded.pass:q-submit-rebuild: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-submit-rebuild: The `int refresh()` example prints `submit(this::refresh).get() = 120`, and the prose says `Both fit, and the one whose method returns a value is more specific` for an exact reference (one declaration, not generic, no varargs), which matches the single `int rebuild()`.
recorded.prompt:q-flush-overload: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-flush-overload: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-flush-overload: Adding `int refresh(boolean force)` yields `error: reference to submit is ambiguous`, the summary says `Adding an overload makes every submit(this::m) ambiguous`, and the design note says it `breaks them at their next compile`. The page's example uses `this::refresh`, but the rule is stated generally for inexact references and the fix uses `cache::refresh`.

recorded.outcome:q-ticket-reversed: The opening `Customer::displayName` case (`displayName()` plus `displayName(Locale)`) fails with `cannot infer type-variable(s) T,U`, and the prose explains `Once overloaded, it tells inference nothing. T becomes Object`, which matches title()/title(int).
recorded.prompt:q-format-array: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-format-array: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-format-array: `render.apply("%s/%s", route)` with `BiFunction<String, Object, String> render = String::format` prints `reference: java.util.MissingFormatArgumentException`, and the prose says `the first %s gets the whole array ... and the second finds nothing`; with the stem's `%s ... %d`, the second specifier likewise finds no argument. The page shows the %s/%s case, not %d specifically, but the mechanism carries over directly.
